# Literal and suppressed numbering controls

Independent control generated by `tools/none_numbering_fixture.py` using
python-docx and manually authored numbering XML. All abstracts have distinct
nsid values and are placed before numbering instances. The source passes
standard/extended schema validation. `native.pdf` is the three-page native
native reference; `reference.json` binds source/PDF hashes and
records all 58 visible item labels, markers and first-character positions.

Current observations:

- `none` with literal `>` still paints `>`.
- `none` with `%1` paints no marker; `[%1]` paints `[]`.
- `isLgl` does not force a none-formatted placeholder to become decimal.
- Nested none `%2` references remain empty even from a legal decimal level.
- Bullet levels also contribute no numeric substitution, even under isLgl.
- A deeper reference suppresses the entire label whether that level is defined
  or absent. This differs from Part 1 §17.9.11's reference-only omission.
  Such a level contributes no numeric text when referenced by a descendant.
- Suppression drops level geometry but retains direct/style geometry. The reference application
  uses a tab suffix and an 18pt fallback numbering tab, even with authored
  space/nothing suffixes or different level indents. Earlier custom tabs can
  win; equality at the fallback tab or body indent does not advance.
  Controls cover positive/negative/zero first-line indents, direct/style
  precedence, changed level geometry and custom tabs.

The unit test checks native labels and package preservation through text edits,
splitting, list toggling, reopen and undo. The browser test checks markers and
body text at native positions before/after editing, undo and reopening. Schema
validation is separate from these visual and behavioral checks.
